title: The distinction between living and dying through the Word
english: Regarding the building of towers, they were assigned one voice and one lip, but through great impiety, having been joined together, they no longer had concord. For those who were making [something] from harmony, intending to be impious, they did not do this, their tongues having been divided. And here, indeed, the one praying desires the tongues of those who have voiced concord against him to be divided, the tongues being submerged, that is, becoming invisible. And before this, if it is said, 'to punish' means 'to submerge.' And Paul, knowing that sometimes it is advantageous to have disagreement against the wicked ones, defending himself on the steps, struck against Pharisees and Sadducees.

This can be referred to the [Psalm] 54:10b, 'Behold, I fled away and was distressed in the wilderness,' through the middle of the two verses from 'I waited for God who saves me,' as the 'He divided their tongues' is such a thing: since in the so-called city of God, Jerusalem, they were committing lawlessness and speaking against the truth, committing lawlessness and speaking against the truth, I fled away from it, so as having become in the wilderness called the Church from the Gentiles, to be distressed in it, resting and spending the night among the believers (Ps 54:11-12).

Since all night and with the day they commit lawlessness and speak against [the truth] in the city, as the city would be surrounded by lawlessness and speaking against [the truth] and by the camp coming upon it because of these, lawlessness and speaking against [the truth] reached and upon its walls, the holy apostles guarding it. For they did not leave it, seeing it committing lawlessness and speaking against [the truth], because lawlessness and toil have come against the praiseworthy pleasure in its midst with injustice, as the birth and deceit of those dwelling in it do not cease from its streets, those acting craftily through whom they think wickedly, toiling by taking upon themselves the burden of evil, with lead being thrown against it.

And its streets were to be considered as souls widening themselves for the sake of pleasure, to walk a wide and spacious road, this being a glorious and passive life. And for always remaining in these, the toil concerning evils and the deceit concerning frauds, it makes it so that 'It did not fail from its streets'...
Birth and deceit. Ps 54,14b.15a 'You know my reproach instead of being known by me, who has made my bonds sweet to me, but to the rest of the disciples nourishing me with good works.'

Ps 54,16bc Someone of the ancients said that those descending into Hades alone are those having received the instruction of the divine teachings. For the taste of the words of life is dead; those living thus descend into Hades. For those living without the common life do not descend into Hades as becoming a body there, for no one has the common life there. Since neither Judas nor all the people of the Jews had received the instruction of the law and the prophets, they descend into Hades with death coming upon them, living according to sin. Consequently, the one approaching is also said in the verse: 'That wickedness is in their sojournings, in their midst.' For even if they had experience of the life-giving writings, they did not dwell but sojourned in them, having wickedness in their midst, that is, in the ruling principle; for it is said that the wickedness is in the midst of the animal.

Ps 54,17 'I cried to God and had my voice heard by the Lord.' For only he who has cried to God is heard by the Lord. For not everyone crying to God shouts; concerning the Sodomites it is written, 'The voice of Sodom and Gomorrah has been filled up,' not having cried to God.

Ps 54,18 Since the narration of a pious man is wisdom throughout, a pious man and narrating wisdom throughout, the psalmist says: 'The evening sets for me the things of wickedness and the extinguished light of the ungodly, but the sun of righteousness rises for me as to make it in the morning; having become one having reached its noon, I will narrate the things of the aforementioned evening and of the previously foretold morning and of the aforementioned noon; and my announcing, God hears the voice of me, accepting and—if so—rejoicing at my voice which has narrated everything.'

Ps 54,20b He says that God exists before the ages but not having existed. For if he had said 'having existed,' he himself, being the beginning, would have existed previously by some measured interval. Because of this, he is not 'The Existing One,' setting his existence as beginningless and eternal, but because of the 'Before the ages' beginning.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The misuse of the Word and the judgment of the unfaithful
english: Being cast down from the existence of the ages. But it is necessary to hear from the ages how the creatures are being diminished. And the Savior is eternal, being from eternity, before the ages, so that even the ages themselves have come to be through him. And Paul says, 'And he himself is before all things' (2 Cor 5:19). The one existing is the same as the one before all things; for it is not that he has come to be before all things. And regarding the Savior, 'Before Abraham was, I am' (John 8:58), not 'I was' or 'I have been', but 'I am'.

Regarding sins, some are difficult and incurable, others are curable (Ps 54:20). Concerning the curable, there is found an exchange: the sacrifice brought up for sins, but also almsgiving and fasting with prayer (for these things rescue from death). But for the incurable of those who have sinned, there is no exchange to lay down as a ransom and a savior. For if a man sins against a man and they pray for him, there is an exchange for these; but if [he sins] against the Lord God, who will pray for him? For there is no exchange for such things.

He stretched out his hand to repay those who worked what was deserved (Ps 54:21). Since traitors and murderers of Christ have become unchangeable and madmen, they are worthy to fall under punishment as those who failed. They were captured by the Romans so that they might be stripped of their manhood and driven out of the nurtured land which they had never belonged to any other. Nor were they accepted back to their fatherland. For they profaned the covenant of God, not only by not adhering to it but also by rejecting the one prophesied under it. Perhaps also, even though the covenant was destined to be kept according to the sensible until the time came when it had to pass from the one according to the flesh to the one according to the spirit, by remaining in the typical worship, they profaned his covenant. Therefore, also, stretching out his punishing hand, he repaid them so that his wrath might reach them to the end, by which they were divided, no longer gathered together in his land, but scattered in every land. These things the wrath of the face of God brought upon them, since when his face shone and appeared, they did not receive it (Ps 54:22). For they were considered to be smooth and without fault because of their hypocrisy...

To seek out missiles like destructive ones and full of gall. For those interpreting even concerning God do not do so correctly; God has drawn near to their own heart, coming down with men, bringing forth words like oil being poured out and loosening the pains of those who suffer. But for those who despise them, the words concerning oil are found to be missiles, striking those who despise them. Often, regarding the striking, there is the metaphor of the arrow, and arrow and missile are the same according to the subject.

Regarding Psalm 54:24a, God does not give a stable place to the righteous, but those who have profaned his covenant he casts into a pit of destruction, contrary to the wells from which the Word protects life and incorruption from drinking. Perhaps 'pit of destruction' means the abyss into which those having been corrupted in their mind are brought down by his vote and are handed over by his judgment.

Regarding Psalm 54:24b–d, He does not wish that the Jews, who exist from before the ages, should be humbled by God. For they fell against the will of the Only-begotten, not fearing God but also profaning his covenant. And he says 'men of blood' concerning those saying, 'His blood is upon us and upon our children,' being guilty of all the blood of the righteous poured out upon the earth. And they themselves are men of guile, always approaching the Savior and the saints deceitfully. He does not wish that for these, even for half of their days, they should overtake [death]. For after they turned away from the day consisting for themselves from the brightness of the true light, having conceived a day of illumination through mythical traditions, it is evil that in this their days be filled; he intercedes that, in the intervening of their days, lest they should reach even half of their days, the sun of righteousness should set for them, so that they might become in the day of the Lord. And regarding the word 'let him force such things'; since in life the impious, dwelling in unrepentant resolve, do many evils, fearing them, it is worthy that, as human life is in the middle, they snatch away life so that for a few sins and not many they might be punished. Of these, he says, not being divided, 'I lay my expectation and hope upon you, O Lord.'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Partial vs Perfect Knowledge and the Soul's Preparation
english: The scripture arranges the idea of being trampled with contempt, just as it is said of the chaff on the threshing floor, 'They throw it out' (Ps 55:2). To be trampled by men and concerning the one devaluing Christ, it has been written: 'How severe a punishment do you think the one who has trampled the Son of God will deserve?' (Hebrews 10:29). And the holy one, being devalued by a man through foolishness, according to the [scripture] 'Where is your jealousy and zeal among you, and do you walk according to man?' (1 Corinthians 3:3), deserves to be shown mercy by God. But this [man] is an unceasing, murderous enemy who crushes the day of life of the righteous by warring, not desiring to be peaceful in any measure. And since in the parable of the weeds (Matt 13:24) the sower of these has been interpreted as the evil man, the devil, stand firm despite what has been said about him.

From this doing, he says, perhaps having fallen from a higher day and life, they have come upon my enemies (Ps 55:3). God saves those who have fallen into wickedness freely, receiving nothing from them (Ps 55:8). For he says, 'Behold, you were struck by your sins and you shall not be redeemed with silver' (Ps 55:8), being saved not by works but by grace. Indeed, 'above nothing' signifies that they are not given salvation above anything else.
The voice growing bold before God (Ps 55:9). For the living one, not by sin but by God, through these works, makes his life manifest to God, announcing it through disposition and practice.

The word brought forth upon God and through God is praiseworthy, likewise also the discourse. But he argues from a parallel against the same word and the discourse, or sets such comparisons one upon another. Since the word is a part of the discourse, the one being led into godliness, if perhaps unable to participate in the most full discourse, begins from a word, that is, a partial discourse. Care [not]; first the word of the Lord comes upon Jeremiah (Jer 1:9), and after this, the discourse of the Lord comes to him; and in Isaiah, he says, 'Hear, O word of the Lord, you who tremble at his discourse' (Isa 66:2). But the word of the Lord is heard in the one occurring through him in the introduction. If anyone should object, saying that it is given to those being evangelized...

With much power, those who know and prophesy partially now receive a word toward the coming knowledge and teaching, as the perfect word is being given to them and the perfect knowledge is shining upon them as if the partial were being abolished. He who accepts both the introduction and the full bestowal of the word praises God with word and discourse (Ps 55:12).

Regarding the flesh, he says that the man who has the mindset of the flesh is an enemy to God, not being subject to the law of God. For he who becomes [one] in this flesh is not able to please God. He fears lest he who becomes [one] in the spirit should do to him, as having killed the works of the flesh; for he has not truly hoped in God (Ps 55:13).

He who prays does not stand in harmony with those to whom he is promised through prayer, but holds within himself the prayers of praise to render to God. And prayers of praise are those concerning praise; for just as someone prays to do or to render this or that to God, so someone prays to praise God (Ps 55:14ab).

And since mourning and the falling of tears follow the one dying, no one mourns the one dead according to the soul except himself, fittingly after the soul has been snatched from the death of the intellect of ignorance concerning God and his eyes have been freed from tears. He snatched his feet from slipping, having shod them with a shoe that lifts up and makes them above the earth. For God says, 'I have shod you with hyacinth.' And the hyacinth, imitating the body of the heaven, shows the soul being colored with the heavenly, with a shoe not being any other than the preparation of the Gospel. Since the one shod is being lifted up, there follows the being snatched from slipping, concerning the feet being snatched from the matter (Ps 55:14c).

Someone is snatched from the aforementioned harmful things in order to please God, living and having been enlightened. For he who pleases God does this while living in light; and he lives and has been enlightened, everyone partaking of God; for he himself, being life, is the light of men, according to the scripture: 'And the life was the light of men' (John 1:4).
The doubling shows that both in this life and in the future we need the mercy of God (Ps 56:2a–c). And he calls the divine protection the shadow of wings.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
